messages:
Samira (People Ops): Kicking off a follow-up thread from today's all-hands Q&A about leveling, comp, and a couple of process clarifications. Post quick Qs or requests here and we'll answer.
Ravi (Eng): Thx. Short one: is there a hard freeze on promotions during hiring pause? managers are anxious.
Maya (People Ops): No hard freeze. Promotions are evaluated on impact, not hiring status. That said, some orgs may have constrained comp pools; managers will be notified during calibration if limits apply.
Jules: Will the promotion decision note include concrete growth areas for non-selected candidates?
Samira (People Ops): Yes 1) managers provide outcome + 2-3 actionable development items, 2) people can request a follow-up 1:1 with manager within 14 days.
Camila: Any changes to the self-nomination process vs last year?
Maya (People Ops): Streamlined form: one summary field, attachments for artifacts, and a checkbox confirming manager has reviewed. We'll share the form link when live.
Tess: Can ICs attach user/customer praise as evidence? is that weighted similarly to metrics?
Maya (People Ops): Absolutely. We weigh qualitative and quantitative evidence. Include both if available; a customer letter + impact metric is strong.
Ravi (Eng): For cross-functional contributors (design/eng), which manager writes the endorsement?
Samira (People Ops): Endorsement should come from the manager of the role the employee is promoted into (or current manager if unclear). If multiple managers, add short lines from each.
Jules: About equity refreshers 1) is there a refresh guideline by level? 2) timing?
Maya (People Ops): Typical guidelines: L4->L5 ~10-20% refresh, L5->L6 larger bands. Refreshes are issued with promotion notifications and may be subject to board approval for senior levels.
Camila: Will salary band ranges be public to all employees or manager-only?
Samira (People Ops): We'll publish band ranges to employees (min / midpoint / max) along with a short explainer doc on how to interpret them.
HR Bot: Note: Promotion window opens 2026-09-10; form available at https://redwood.internal/promote.
Tess: Request: can People Ops provide a 1-page manager script for delivering promotion/no-promotion conversations? helps reduce awkwardness.
Maya (People Ops): Good idea 1) we'll draft a 1-page script + sample language for development conversations and upload by Sep 3.
Ravi (Eng): One edge case: employee on international assignment with differing title conventions. Who handles leveling?
Samira (People Ops): Leveling follows the home org's ladder; comp conversion handled by payroll and comp. Managers should note assignment context in the submission.
Jules: Appeals process quick summary? I missed that slide.
Maya (People Ops): Appeal steps: 1) talk to manager within 14 days, 2) if unresolved, submit appeal form within 21 days, 3) People Ops convenes an independent panel. SLA ~21 days for adjudication.
Camila: Will we get anonymized promotion metrics by org for fairness checks?
Samira (People Ops): Yes 1) after calibration we'll share org-level aggregates (counts by level/gender/region where available). No individual names.
Tess: Any update on bonus timing? some folks thought it was Sept.
Samira (People Ops): Annual bonus payout is scheduled for Nov 1. We'll post the final memo in the handbook.
Ravi (Eng): Thanks 1) final ask: can People Ops hold a 30-min office hour for managers to run candidate packages by you before submission?
Maya (People Ops): Yep 1) we'll schedule 3 office hours in the two weeks before the window and post sign-ups.
HR Bot: People Ops docs will be published to https://redwood.internal/people-resources on 2026-09-02 15:00 UTC.
Samira (People Ops): Great thread 1) we'll pin the resources and templates here once live. If you'd like an example manager note, ping me and I'll share a redacted sample. :v:
